Comparisons with experimental constraints from BaBar, Belle and Belle II restrict the allowed parameter space. We also identify kinematic regions where power-suppressed contributions exceed the leading terms, highlighting limitations of the HQE. Together, these studies advance the theoretical understanding of heavy-hadron lifetimes, strengthen the bridge between precision flavour physics and physics beyond the SM, and open new avenues for probing the interplay between heavy-quark dynamics and the dark sector.

papers.title: Is there gluonium in the $η^\prime$? The flavour structure of $η$ and $η^\prime$ mixing in radiative $V\to Pγ$ and $P\to Vγ$ decays
papers.abstract: Radiative $V\to Pγ$ and $P\to Vγ$ decays are conventionally described using constituent-quark mass differences and phenomenological wavefunction-overlap factors as sources of flavour-symmetry breaking. We investigate whether the overlap factors can instead be understood as the effect of mixing of the $η$ and $η^\prime$ with an additional pseudoscalar state, described by an $SO(4)$ rotation among four basis states. A global fit to current data yields a significantly better description than the corresponding three-state limit without overlap factors, while preserving the established $η$-$η^\prime$ and vector-meson mixing angles, and shows that the additional state mixes predominantly with the non-strange component. The conventional overlap-factor description is recovered exactly as the special case in which this mixing is purely non-strange. The non-strange pattern disfavours both a flavour-singlet admixture, as expected from mixing with a pseudoscalar glueball, and the gluonium scenario considered in previous analyses. Radiative decays therefore provide no compelling evidence for gluonium in the $η^\prime$, and the overlap factors are better interpreted in terms of a radially excited non-strange state.

papers.title: Quantum Veto Parton Shower Algorithm in the Conformal Window
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum veto parton shower algorithm for a confining dark sector with gauge symmetry $\mathrm{SU}(3)_D \times \mathrm{U}(1)_D$ operating in the conformal window ($N_C = 3$, $N_F = 12$). The non-Abelian gauge coupling exhibits two-loop running toward an infrared fixed point before decoupling at a finite dark-quark mass threshold, while the dark quarks carry non-degenerate $\mathrm{U}(1)_D$ charges with unitary flavor mixing between the interaction and mass bases. Shower evolution proceeds coherently in the interaction basis, with states prepared and measured in the mass basis. Compared with the classical Markovian shower, the flavor-coherent quantum simulation produces a significantly enhanced zero-emission rate, and a characteristic U-shaped mass-eigenstate spectrum. Furthermore, energy-energy correlators exhibit approximate linearity in the double-logarithmic coordinates over an intermediate angular range, suggesting power-law scaling in that region. This framework demonstrates the capability of quantum algorithms to capture multi-flavor quantum interference in strongly interacting hidden sectors.

papers.title: Probing the Energy Evolution and Hadronic Cascade Time Dependence of Forward-Backward Multiplicity Correlations in pp Collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 0.9$--$13.6$~TeV with AMPT
papers.abstract: Forward-backward (FB) multiplicity correlations are studied in proton--proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies of $\sqrt{s} = 0.9$, $2.76$, $5.02$, $7$, $13$, and $13.6$~TeV using the AMPT model in its default (DF) and string melting (SM) configurations. The coefficient $b_{\rm corr}$ is obtained for windows separated in pseudorapidity and azimuth, and its variation with the pseudorapidity gap, window width, collision energy, transverse momentum interval, and hadronic cascade time $τ_{\rm HC}$ is investigated. The simulated results are compared with the available ALICE measurements, and the model is validated against experimental pseudorapidity densities and charged-pion transverse momentum spectra. The correlation strength is found to decrease gradually with increasing pseudorapidity gap while retaining a substantial pedestal, to rise non-linearly with the window width, and to increase substantially with collision energy. The DF configuration yields systematically larger values of $b_{\rm corr}$ than the SM configuration, while the SM configuration provides the better description of the ALICE data at $0.9$ and $2.76$~TeV and the DF configuration at $7$~TeV. In the lowest transverse momentum intervals the deviations from the data are largest for both configurations. The hadronic cascade time is varied within the SM configuration over $τ_{\rm HC} = 0.6$, $5$, $15$, and $30$~fm/$c$. A monotonic reduction of $b_{\rm corr}$ with increasing $τ_{\rm HC}$ is observed at all energies and for all window widths, with the ordering of the curves preserved throughout. The effect is modest but statistically significant. These results indicate that the FB correlation strength is primarily imprinted at the partonic stage and only mildly diluted by the subsequent hadronic evolution.

papers.title: alpha_s from hadron multiplicities: an updated analysis
papers.abstract: Exploring the anomalous dimensions, resummed through next-to-next-to-leading-logarithmic order, we study the first Mellin moments D_{q,g}(μ^2) of the quark and gluon fragmentation functions, which correspond to the average hadron multiplicities in jets initiated by quarks and gluons, respectively. By fitting the world data on D_{q,g}(μ^2) for charged hadrons measured in e^+e^- annihilation, we find a good agreement with the data and obtain the following value for the strong force coupling α_s^{(5)}(M_Z)=0.1177+0.0027-0.0025.

papers.title: Where are the higher excited $B$ and $B_s$ mesons with coupled-channel effects?
papers.abstract: Inspired by the newly observed $B_{s0}^*(5700)^0$, whose mass agrees well with our previous unquenched prediction for $B_s(1^3P_0)$ [Phys.~Rev.~D \textbf{109}, 116006 (2024)], we study the mass spectra and OZI-allowed two-body strong decays of the higher $3S$-, $2P$-, $2D$-, and $1F$-wave $B$ and $B_s$ mesons in the same unquenched quark model. Our results show that coupled-channel effects significantly lower the masses and modify the relative level spacings. The scalar state $B(2^3P_0)$ is strongly affected: its mass is lowered well below the quenched quark model predictions, and it mainly decays into $Bπ$. Furthermore, the mass ordering of the vector states $B(2^3D_1)$ and $B(3^3S_1)$ is reversed, and the lighter $B(2^3D_1)$ state mainly decays into $B_1(5721)π$. To test these results, the $B(2^3P_0)$ and $B(2^3D_1)$ states are worth searching for in the $Bπ$ and $B_1(5721)π$ channels, respectively. In addition, some higher excitations are predicted to be relatively narrow and can be searched for in the $B^{(*)}π$, $B^{(*)}K$, $B_1(5721)π/K$, and $B_2^*(5747)π/K$ channels. These predictions provide useful references for future experimental searches and help clarify the role of coupled-channel effects in the heavy-light meson spectrum.

papers.title: Summary of Aspen discussions on perturbative uncertainties beyond 7-point variations
papers.abstract: This writeup elaborates on constructive discussions which took place at the Aspen Center for Physics, Aug - Sep 2024, during the program "Tightening the gap between scattering amplitudes and events at the LHC at higher orders". Building on already existing theoretical understanding from the study of scattering amplitudes and resummations at higher orders, we suggest to complement standard 7-point renormalisation- and factorisation-scale variations by additional estimates of missing higher-order terms which are known to be present in the perturbative series. We also summarise a recent proposal for at least one way that non-Gaussian theory uncertainties might be treated within a frequentist framework. This may help to provide more robust and comprehensive uncertainty estimates for experimental and phenomenological applications of perturbative calculations.

papers.title: Solar Neutrino Signals and Capture-Annihilation Equilibrium of SU(5) Neutralino Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Motivated by IceCube solar searches, we investigate neutralino dark matter in supersymmetric SU(5) with nonuniversal gaugino masses. Combining micrOMEGAs relic abundances with DarkSUSY calculations, we develop a consistent picture of solar neutrino and muon signals from thermal neutralino subcomponents. We identify how local abundance, neutralino composition, and capture-annihilation equilibrium shape these signals beyond simple scaling with the dark matter fraction. Integrated fluxes and representative benchmarks connect these predictions to published IceCube reference limits. Our results provide a framework for interpreting solar searches and assessing the signals of subdominant neutralino dark matter.

papers.title: $U$-spin sum rules in charmed baryon decays beyond the $U$-spin limit
papers.abstract: $U$-spin symmetry is an important flavor symmetry in studying charmed hadron weak decays. However, the sizeable $U$-spin breaking limits the predictive power of $U$-spin symmetry. In this work, we derive dozens of rate and decay parameter $U$-spin sum rules for charmed baryon decays beyond the exact $U$-spin symmetry limit. These sum rules provide tests of flavor symmetry up to the first-order $U$-spin breaking in the charmed baryon sector.

papers.title: Dynamical resonances $Λ(1405)$, $Λ(1670)$, and $f_0(980)$ in the process $Λ_c^+ \to p K^+ K^-$
papers.abstract: Motivated by new BESIII measurements of the singly Cabibbo-suppressed process $Λ_c^+ \to p K^+ K^- $, we investigate the $Λ_c^+ \to p K^+ K^-$ reaction by taking into account contributions from the low-lying excited baryons $Λ(1405)$ and $Λ(1670)$, which are dynamically generated via the $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson-octet baryon interaction. In addition, contributions from the light scalar mesons $f_0(980)/a_0(980)$ dynamically generated via the $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson-pseudoscalar meson interaction, as well as the vector meson $φ(1020)$, are also considered. The theoretical calculations could reproduce the invariant mass distributions of $K^- p$ and $K^+K^-$ measured by the BESIII Collaboration well. Specifically, a near-threshold enhancement and a cusp structure around 1670~MeV in the $pK^-$ invariant mass spectrum are obtained, which are associated with the $Λ(1405)$ and $Λ(1670)$ resonances, respectively. Furthermore, contributions from the scalar meson $f_0(980)$ and vector meson $φ(1020)$ are clearly observed in the $K^+ K^-$ invariant mass distribution. Future high-precision measurements by the BESIII, Belle II, and the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility experiments will substantially deepen our understanding of the intrinsic properties of the low-lying excited $Λ$ states and the $f_0(980)/a_0(980)$ meson.

papers.title: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe
papers.abstract: We study a flat three-torus universe whose contraction is turned around by the negative Casimir energy of Standard Model fields. The trace anomaly forbids conformal matter alone to turn an anisotropic universe around, so matter with $w<1/3$, most cheaply a positive potential, must supply the negative trace; with antiperiodic fermions the Standard Model supplies the negative energy, and the universe turns at an edge of 722 reduced Planck lengths. There the Higgs quartic coupling is negative, but zero-point fluctuations of the constant gauge modes confine the Higgs zero mode down to a finite-volume threshold $λ_c\approx-0.012$, below the Standard Model value $-0.0098$. The Higgs survives with probability above $1/2$ for a top-quark pole mass below $172.96$ GeV ($\bar m_t<163.16$ GeV; $α_s(M_Z)=0.1180$), and with probability $\approx0.7$ for current data, given a curvature coupling $ξ_H\gtrsim0.08$ at the scale $\bar M_{\mathrm{P}}/722$. The turning point can hold only about five quanta of the lowest modes, whereas a reheating coupling in a time-symmetric past would produce radiation exceeding the Casimir energy by at least $10^{94}$, so we read the turn as a beginning rather than a bounce. Negative Casimir energy cannot hold the shape of the torus: the shape state can be real at most once, and for a real Gaussian state survival of the shape on both branches with $90\%$ probability requires that moment to lie within $0.35$ Hubble times of the turn. The natural state, real at the turn, freezes the torus into a nearly rectangular box whose sides typically differ by $16$-$18\%$. The microwave background can read this fossil only if the shortest cycle lies between $0.985$ and about $1.04$ last-scattering diameters. A top-quark pole mass above $173.7$ GeV, within reach of FCC-ee, would exclude this beginning (Bayes factor $\lesssim0.03$).

papers.title: Recent Advances in Transverse-Momentum--Dependent Distributions in Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Unraveling the three-dimensional structure of hadrons is a central objective in modern nuclear and particle physics. Transverse Momentum Dependent parton distributions (TMDs) provide crucial insights into the interplay between partonic transverse motion and spin, and are indispensable for describing a wide range of high-energy processes at facilities such as JLab, COMPASS, the LHC, and the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider. In recent years, significant progress has been made in accessing TMDs from lattice QCD using novel approaches. Methods based on ratios of Mellin moments, large-momentum effective theory (LaMET), and Coulomb-gauge techniques have enabled first-principles investigations of the Collins-Soper kernel, intrinsic soft functions, TMD wave functions, and TMDPDFs. Recent lattice results for both unpolarized and spin-dependent distributions, including the Boer-Mulders function, demonstrate the feasibility of extracting transverse-momentum--dependent information directly from QCD. This paper reviews recent advances in lattice-QCD studies of TMDs, outlines remaining challenges such as continuum and infinite-momentum extrapolations, and discusses future directions toward precision determinations of hadron structure in three dimensions.

papers.title: Probing dark-matter scenarios of Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+M_X$ with $K^+\to π^+ M_X$ decays
papers.abstract: The hypothesis of top-philic dark matter as the origin of the Belle II excess events in $B\to K M_X$ decays has direct impact on $K\to πM_X$ decays: Both of these decays proceed via loop diagrams~with a top quark emitting some mediator field $R$ and the subsequent decay of $R$ into a pair of dark-matter fermions $\barχχ$. The Belle II results on $B\to K M_X$ allowed us to extract the parameters of the mediator $R$ with reasonable accuracy, whereas the sensitivity to the fermion mass $m_χ$ proved to be rather low. In contrast to $B\to K M_X$ decays, the $K\to πM_X$ decays exhibit a strong sensitivity to $m_χ$; therefore, if - upon reducing theoretical and experimental uncertainties - the tension between standard-model predictions for the $K\toπM_X$ decays and the most recent NA62 measurements becomes pronounced the latter decays may either enable the extraction of the value of $m_χ$ or provide a lower limit on~$m_χ$.

papers.title: Global analyses of PDFs in the precision era
papers.abstract: Parton distribution functions or PDFs are determined through global fits to an ever-increasing array of data, including deep-inelastic scattering at fixed-target experiments and HERA, and hadron collisions at the Tevatron and LHC. As the dataset has expanded, theoretical accuracy has improved from partial next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) coverage about 20 years ago to approximate N$^3$LO global fits today. The fitting collaborations must reconcile these complex calculations and data analyses while ensuring that quoted PDF uncertainty bands remain reliable.

papers.title: Common origin of the Belle-BESIII line-shape difference of $Λ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$, $D_s D_{s1}$ and $D_s D_{s2}^*$ from $e^+ e^-$ annihilation
papers.abstract: The longstanding Belle--BESIII discrepancies in the $e^+e^-\toΛ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$, $D_sD_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_sD_{s2}^{*}(2573)$ line shapes remain an unresolved puzzle, with enhancements observed by Belle that are absent or much weaker in the BESIII measurements. In this work, we propose a new mechanism based on the radiative production of higher charmonia to explain these differences. Such processes may contribute to Belle's initial-state radiation samples, and the luminosity normalization increases their contribution to the extracted cross sections. With the vector contributions scaled by BESIII data, a pseudoscalar charmonium $η_c(6S)$ contribution can describe the baryonic enhancement, while an introduced $χ_{c2}(5P)$ contribution can describe the enhancements in both meson channels. This mechanism offers a possible common explanation for these differences and, as a bonus, suggests a way to search for missing higher charmonia at Belle II.

papers.title: Tensor-polarized gluon distribution \texorpdfstring{$h_{1TT}^{g}$}{h1TTg} in the deuteron: QCD evolution and Drell-Yan phenomenology
papers.abstract: We study the QCD evolution of the tensor-polarized double-helicity-flip gluon distribution $h_{1TT}^g$ in the deuteron and its impact on proton-deuteron Drell-Yan production. The nonperturbative input is taken from the spin-1 spectator model and evolved at leading order with the autonomous gluon evolution equation. The uncertainty of the model fit is propagated to the tensor-polarized cross-section difference and the asymmetry $A_{E_{xy}}$ using an ensemble of 100 replicas. Compared with the earlier benchmark estimate based on a longitudinally polarized gluon distribution, the evolved spectator-model input gives smaller cross sections in most of the kinematic region and a much stronger decrease of $|A_{E_{xy}}|$ with $Q^2$. At sufficiently large center-of-mass energy, the asymmetry varies only slowly with $\sqrt{s}$, whereas the low-$\sqrt{s}$ and large-$Q^2$ regions probe the poorly constrained large-$x$ tail of the model. We also evolve the tensor-polarized gluon distribution $f_{1LL}^g$ in the coupled singlet-gluon system and assess its contribution to the reference cross-section sum. Its effect remains moderate in the kinematic region where the spectator-model prediction is under reasonable control.

papers.title: Ultra-relativistic freeze-out of fermion dark matter through a heavy scalar mediator
papers.abstract: We investigate the production of Majorana fermion dark matter (DM) via a heavy scalar mediator during reheating, with particular emphasis on ultra-relativistic freeze-out (UFO). Depending on the mediator mass, interaction strengths, and reheating temperature, we identify three distinct production regimes: freeze-in, WIMP-like freeze-out, and UFO, all of which can account for the observed DM relic abundance. In the UFO regime, significant DM production can persist after chemical decoupling, while entropy injection during reheating simultaneously dilutes the DM yield. An accurate determination of the final relic abundance therefore requires a consistent treatment of both continued production and entropy dilution. We further examine the impact of scalar cubic interactions and find that they modify the boundaries between the different production regimes and reshape the relic-density contours. In particular, the results are more sensitive to the cubic coupling involving the mediator and the light scalar than to the heavy-scalar self-coupling.

papers.title: Forward $χ_c$ production in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions within the CGC+NRQCD framework
papers.abstract: We study the forward $χ_{cJ}$ production in the low $p_{\perp}$ region in proton-proton $(pp)$ and proton-nucleus $(pA)$ collisions at the LHC within the framework of non-relativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization and the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective field theory. Incorporating the small-$x$ gluonic evolution via the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov equation with various initial conditions, we systematically analyze the cross section ratio $R_{χ_{c}}=σ_{χ_{c2}}/σ_{χ_{c1}}$, and find that the theoretical predictions weakly depend on these inputs. Our predictions align well with the LHCb measurements for $p\mathrm{Pb}$ collisions, however, overshoot those for $pp$ collisions. We further investigate the feed down fractions $F_{χ_{c1,2}\to J/ψ}=σ_{χ_{c1,2}\to J/ψ}/σ_{J/ψ}$. We notice that with the experimental measurement of prompt $J/ψ$ cross section as inputs in the denominator the CGC+NRQCD predictions broadly match the data when choosing the standard McLerran-Venugopalan initial conditions. In contrast, implementing purely theoretical CGC+NRQCD predictions for both $J/ψ$ and $χ_{c}$ production yield systematic discrepancies across all tested parameters. This highlights a persistent challenge in achieving a simultaneous, unified description of $χ_{c}$ and prompt $J/ψ$ production within the current framework.

papers.title: Floquet Instability of Photon-Axion Conversion
papers.abstract: The discovery of axions would provide evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we investigate axion-photon conversion in the presence of a background magnetic field with simultaneous spatial and temporal periodicity. By performing a Lorentz transformation, the coupled axion-photon system is mapped onto a time-periodic linear system that can be analyzed using Floquet theorem. We find unstable modes associated with resonant crossing between Floquet replicas. The resulting complex Floquet exponents lead to exponentially growing modes, which we identify as a Floquet instability. Then, we determine the parameter regions in which this instability appears in a perturbative analysis. We further show that the Floquet instability enhances the axion-field amplitude generated from an initial photon field. Our results demonstrate that spatiotemporally periodic magnetic backgrounds provide a distinct mechanism for modifying axion-photon conversion through Floquet instability.

papers.title: Phenomenology of Spontaneous CP-violation in 2HDMs
papers.abstract: Spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) provides an attractive possibility for explaining the origin of CP violation and the observed CP-violating phenomena in the quark sector. We investigate SCPV in the two-Higgs-doublet model as one of its simplest realizations, in which the additional Higgs bosons are necessarily non-decoupling and flavor misalignment in the Yukawa sector is required. The non-decoupling Higgs sector predicts sizable deviations from the Standard Model predictions even in the Higgs alignment limit: the decay rates of the discovered Higgs boson into $γγ$ and $Zγ$ can deviate by at least about $-10\%$ and $-4\%$, respectively, while the trilinear Higgs self-coupling can receive $\mathcal{O}(100)\%$ corrections. We consider a scenario in which the down-type quark and charged-lepton Yukawa matrices are flavor aligned, while flavor-violating interactions are allowed in the up-type quark sector to reproduce the Kobayashi-Maskawa phase. We explore the viable parameter space by imposing theoretical constraints together with experimental constraints from electroweak precision observables, flavor measurements, electric dipole moments, and LHC data. We find that a sizable flavor-violating top-charm Yukawa coupling remains allowed, giving rise to distinctive LHC signatures, including same-sign top-quark and three-top production as well as scalar cascade decays. We also find that the deviation in the trilinear Higgs self-coupling is correlated with the decay patterns of the additional neutral Higgs bosons, providing a connection between precision Higgs measurements and direct searches for the additional Higgs bosons. Our results demonstrate the importance of combining searches for additional Higgs bosons with precision Higgs measurements, complemented by flavor and electric-dipole-moment experiments, to probe SCPV.

papers.title: Collider event distances from the phase space sphere
papers.abstract: Can the distribution of collider events in phase space be used to distinguish the processes that produced them? We present a distance-based classification method that uses the global topology of Lorentz-invariant phase space and retains reconstructed masses. To tackle particularly challenging classification tasks that may benefit from higher event resolution, we develop a polynomial-time approximation to compute the distances. The resulting classifiers achieve strong discrimination across several simulated benchmarks, including fully hadronic four-top production against $t\bar t+\text{jets}$.

papers.title: Electric Flux as a Criterion for String Breaking and Schwinger Pair Production
papers.abstract: We define string breaking by the midpoint electric field falling to half a flux unit. In the massive Schwinger model, an energy balance between intact string and screened configuration predicts this separation using only vacuum observables and meson masses as input. We observe numerically that this half flux point corresponds to equal weights of the two configurations thus explaining the observed peak of the entanglement entropy as maximal uncertainty of the binary flux. The same binary uncertainty explains the entanglement peak at the vacuum transition. Near breaking, screening organizes part of the spatial entanglement between the string interior and exterior into a nearly maximally entangled bit. Within the selected flux sectors, this approximate encoded Bell pair records whether the flux is screened and nearly separates from the remaining correlations. The vacuum transition exhibits the same structure. The string and the $θ$-vacuum reveal a matching structure of the capacity of entanglement minimum at their transition point, linking their entanglement spectra. The transition rearranges degrees of freedom coherently as revealed by the entanglement asymmetry and Robustness of Magic of disjoint subregions. Finally, we construct the $θ$-vacuum and string wavefunctions with high fidelity using a restricted Boltzmann machine ansatz.

papers.title: BeAGLE++: A modern modular framework for eA physics at the EIC
papers.abstract: We present the Benchmark eA Generator for LEptoproduction (BeAGLE++), a next-generation, general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator for high-energy lepton-nucleus collisions and the successor to BeAGLE. The framework incorporates a formation-zone intranuclear cascade to describe hadronic final-state interactions (FSIs), followed by statistical de-excitation of the residual nucleus. Compared with the legacy implementation, the BeAGLE++ cascade introduces a discrete time-ordered treatment of hadronic interactions and light-cluster production during intranuclear transport. Comparisons with E665 measurements and legacy BeAGLE calculations show broad agreement for selected observables, while revealing differences in final states sensitive to FSIs. These differences provide opportunities to assess the model dependence of nuclear-breakup predictions and constrain the underlying cascade dynamics. With its modular architecture, BeAGLE++ provides a flexible simulation framework for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) and a platform for developing and testing new physics models against existing data and future EIC measurements.

papers.title: Angular Momentum Loss at Fourth Post-Minkowskian Order
papers.abstract: We calculate the total loss of angular momentum for a gravitational scattering of two non-spinning point-like objects at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$. Our methodology combines use of both amplitudes and worldline-based methods. We derive the integrand from two copies of the gravitational waveform with cuts on massive lines arising naturally from the worldline. We then glue these two copies and evaluate the resulting phase-space integrals using reverse unitarity, in the amplitudes spirit. We obtain separately the radiated angular momentum and the static contribution that, at this order, is entirely determined by the initial shear and the linear memory. Combining these two terms, we derive relativistic expressions for the angular momentum loss and for the infrared-finite component of the mass dipole loss, which in the low-velocity limit match results available in the literature. We also use this result to derive the conservative deflection angle at $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$ and first self-force order.

papers.title: Breaking the axion abundance-isocurvature relation: Scale invariance and high-scale inflation
papers.abstract: A QCD axion accounting for dark matter through pre-inflationary misalignment is strongly constrained by CMB isocurvature bounds, which place the classic axion window in tension with high-scale inflation. The tension arises because the same decay constant controls both the relic abundance and the primordial axion fluctuations. We show how this link can be broken in a broad class of scale-invariant models, without introducing any dimensionful parameter into the classical action. Rather than imposing a fixed Peccei-Quinn scale, the axion's kinetic normalisation is set by a dynamical field ratio. The resulting field-space metric controls the abundance through its value today and the primordial fluctuations through its value at horizon crossing. A sufficiently large metric during inflation suppresses isocurvature, allowing high-scale inflation in the classic axion window with an untuned misalignment angle and sub-Planckian decay constants. The exact scale and Peccei-Quinn symmetries also enforce a non-turning inflationary attractor, conserving the super-Hubble curvature perturbation and preserving the single-field adiabatic spectrum. We realise the mechanism in the Higgs-Dilaton model by deforming the Peccei-Quinn kinetic term. The same deformation turns the inflaton sector into an $α$-attractor pinned near the Starobinsky point. This explicit realisation has a super-Planckian present decay constant, which places it in the anthropic window, now reopened at high inflationary scales, with an ultralight QCD axion constrained by black-hole superradiance.

papers.title: Measurement of the neutrino cross section across the TeV scale using IceCube data
papers.abstract: Neutrinos interact with matter exclusively through the weak force, resulting in extremely small cross sections that are difficult to measure. At TeV energies, neutrino-nucleon interactions probe the structure of the nucleon in regimes where our knowledge of it is less complete, and signatures of physics beyond the Standard Model could manifest. Recent measurements using collider, atmospheric, and astrophysical neutrinos have begun to explore this regime, but no single measurement has provided precise coverage from sub-TeV to tens of TeV, and uncertainties remain at the level of about 20-40%. Here we present a determination of the muon-neutrino-nucleon charged-current cross sections as a function of energy across 150 GeV-40 TeV using eight years of through-going muon neutrino data collected by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. We measure the average neutrino-antineutrino cross section, enabling direct comparison with previous results, and find, for the first time above 1 TeV, mild indications that the neutrino and antineutrino cross sections can be measured separately. The measured cross sections are consistent with Standard Model predictions and are determined with uncertainties below 20% throughout the explored energy range, achieving the most precise characterization of neutrino-nucleon interactions across the TeV scale to date. These results provide a unified measurement of neutrino-nucleon cross sections in this energy regime, connecting accelerator-based and previous higher-energy neutrino observations - thereby advancing high-energy neutrino physics into the precision era.

papers.title: Multimessenger Probes of Primordial Black Holes with Gravitational Wave and 21 cm Observations
papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from the collapse of curvature perturbations in the early universe are known to have an associated gravitational wave signal sourced by the same scalar perturbations. In this work, we show that there is a complementarity between these gravitational waves and modifications of the 21 cm global signal during the cosmic dark ages due to PBH evaporation. For PBHs in the range $ M_{\rm PBH} \sim 5 \times 10^{13} \, {\rm g} - 10^{17} \, {\rm g}$, there is a correlated signal in gravitational waves in the LISA, deci-Hz, and ground based regimes from $f_{\rm GW} \sim 10^{-3} \, {\rm Hz} - 20 \, {\rm Hz}$ and in the 21 cm global signal from $z \sim 300 - 30$. These observations are entirely independent of each other and within the reach of near-future experiments, making a combined measurement a novel multimessenger probe of primordial physics.

papers.title: Testing Leptogenesis via CP asymmetries in Lepton-Number-Violating $W$ Decays at Colliders
papers.abstract: In principle, searches for CP asymmetries in rare $W$-boson decays can test low-scale leptogenesis in the GeV-scale type-I seesaw with three quasi-degenerate-in-mass heavy right-handed neutrinos. To investigate this, we focus on the lepton-number-violating heavy-neutrino-mediated decay $W^{\pm}\to e^{\pm} e^{\pm} (\bar{q} q')^{\mp}$, with $(\bar{q} q')^+ = (\bar{d}u)^+$ and $(\bar{q} q')^- = (\bar{u}d)^-$. We determine the minimum branching ratio required for a CP asymmetry to be observable at colliders with a given statistical significance. We then perform a numerical scan of the presently-allowed parameter space, also solving the density matrix equations for low-scale leptogenesis, and identify regions where, simultaneously, the present baryon asymmetry of the Universe can be achieved and the collider CP asymmetry for the considered decay is observable at HL-LHC and FCC-hh. We find that these regions are sizeable. A future observation of a CP asymmetry in $W^{\pm}\to e^{\pm} e^{\pm} (\bar{q} q')^{\mp}$ within the regions identified here would provide evidence in favour of low-scale leptogenesis as the origin of the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the Universe.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves as a Probe of Multi-Fluid Cosmologies: General Formalism and the Case of Cosmological Stasis
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) provide a powerful probe of the expansion history of the universe prior to the Big Bang. Indeed, the production of such gravity waves depends on the evolution of first-order scalar perturbations within the early universe, while their subsequent propagation depends on the background equation of state. In this paper we extend previous discussions by studying SIGWs in cosmologies containing multiple fluids. As we shall demonstrate, the gravitational-wave signal within such multi-fluid cosmologies is modified in two distinct ways: not only are there new velocity effects which have no single-fluid analogues, but there are also significant alterations to the subsequent redshifting of modes that enter the horizon before the multi-fluid era ends. Thus SIGWs provide a probe of not only the overall expansion rate within such cosmologies, but also their internal multi-fluid composition. As an example, we then consider the case of gravitational waves arising during an epoch of cosmological stasis. During such an epoch, the abundances of energy components with different equations of state remain constant, thereby giving rise to a universe with a constant effective equation of state which nevertheless remains genuinely multi-fluid despite cosmological expansion. Despite their constant equations of state, we find that such stasis cosmologies also give rise to tensor power spectra and present-day gravitational-wave abundances which are significantly different from those expected within a standard radiation-dominated universe.

papers.title: Impact of Irrep Truncations on Quantum Simulations of QCD
papers.abstract: Quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories with continuous gauge groups require a choice of basis (how states of the gauge theory map to the qubit computational basis) and truncation scheme (which of the infinitely many gauge theory basis states should be omitted in the map to the finite dimensional qubit Hilbert space.) The most common choices are adapted to an electric basis for the gauge theory, where the basis states for each link are associated with irreducible representations of the gauge group. Electric bases and truncations are generally advantageous for preserving gauge symmetries and simulating the strong coupling regime, but their effectiveness in the weak coupling regimes of physical interest are less well understood. In this work, we compute relative probabilities $p(R')/p(R)$ for finding a link in the irreps $R,R'$ in the ground state of SU(3) lattice gauge theory using Euclidean Monte Carlo methods and weak-coupling lattice perturbation theory. The observables that compute these relative probabilities are constructed by introducing seams into an anisotropic lattice, and by a similar construction we are also able to measure relative probabilities of different site singlets (ways that electric flux braids together into a gauge singlet) at each vertex. With these methods we can quantify, for example, the importance of higher electric flux states in the weak coupling ground state. These results directly inform what truncations are needed to accurately capture non-abelian gauge dynamics near the continuum limit.

papers.title: Complete $g^6$ pressure of hot Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: We present the full order $g^6$ term in the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of hot $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory, resolving a problem that has remained open for more than two decades. To achieve this, we evaluate nine previously unknown nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals using the thermal loop-tree duality method with novel local ultraviolet and infrared subtractions, thereby completing the hard-scale contribution to the pressure for general $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$. Combining this result with known chromoelectric and chromomagnetic contributions, available for $N_c=3$, we demonstrate the analytic cancellation of infrared divergences originating from different momentum scales and obtain the complete $O(g^6)$ pressure for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. Our result displays quantitative agreement with data from four-dimensional lattice simulations over a broad range of temperatures, providing a stringent test of the dimensionally reduced effective-field-theory paradigm.

papers.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, perturbatively
papers.abstract: We determine the four-loop hard-scale matching correction to the pressure of the gluon plasma at high temperature. This result completes the long-standing calculation through $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, where $g_s$ is the strong coupling. Our result agrees, within uncertainties, with the value obtained in arXiv:1204.6184 by fitting the perturbative series to continuum-extrapolated lattice data, thereby providing the first direct test of the weak-coupling expansion at this order.

papers.title: Equiprobability Anomaly Detector Using Angular Distributions
papers.abstract: We use the angular distribution of top quark pairs ($t\bar{t}$) in the semileptonic final state $b\bar{b}\,\ellνq\bar{q}'$ to construct an anomaly detector for non-$t\bar{t}$ events. Wigner $D$ functions expand the distribution with coefficients determined by orthogonal series density estimation. Its equiprobable surfaces bin the events, the non-$t\bar{t}$ concentrate at low $t\bar{t}$ density. The separation is quantified by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, which makes connection to variational autoencoders. The performance is comparable to normalizing flows at parton level, but is limited by jet assignments at reconstruction level.

papers.title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
papers.abstract: Hidden sectors are generic in beyond the Standard Model constructions and string compactifications. We consider models featuring hidden sectors that have dark matter candidates. The relic density is set in part by the energy-injecting inflaton branching ratio $B$ to the sector. We develop a general framework to determine the dependence on $B$ for thermalized hidden sectors by defining an effective Planck mass for the Boltzmann equations for the hidden sector degrees of freedom. We apply this framework to several representative examples, including freeze-out/freeze-in WIMPs and multi-component dark matter. We find that the fractional energy density carried by freeze-out relics (in both single and multi-component models) and monopoles produced from second order phase transitions scale as $B^{1/4}$ and thus may lead to an overclosure problem, even with $B \ll 1$. On the other hand, the energy density of freeze-in relics scales as $B^{5/4}$ and is thus cosmologically irrelevant for sufficiently small $B$. Finally, we discuss the cumulative implications of a large number of hidden sectors.

papers.title: Mass, forces, and the dark sector in a Kaluza-Klein model with 6 compact dimensions
papers.abstract: (1) Objective: This study seeks to calculate the meson and baryon masses and to investigate the dynamics within hadrons and lepton pairs by formulating a unified physical framework that, in addition to gravitation, simultaneously incorporates the strong, electromagnetic and weak interactions. (2) Method: A framework inspired by the Standard Model and based on Kaluza-Klein theory is formulated using an extended general-relativistic description in a spacetime of one temporal, three spatial, and six compactified dimensions. The model suggests that excitations, deformations of the 10-dimensional spacetime traveling at light-speed, contribute to mass and distinct spin characteristics in a 4-dimensional setting. Using the electron g-factor, charged-lepton masses, and masses of the proton, neutron, and neutral and charged pion, neutral and charged rho, phi, psi, upsilon mesons, the parameters compactification radius rho, weak interaction coupling alpha_w, strong interaction coupling alpha_s, flavor constants A_i and the antineutrino/neutrino density ratio delta3 are determined and used to compute the masses of the hadrons. (3) Key results: Masses of 102 hadrons are obtained; comparison with data from 71 measurements shows relative errors below 0.05 in 70%, below 0.1 in 89% and below 0.2 in 100%, with a correlation coefficient r=0.997 between the measured and calculated masses. Thirty-one additional hadron masses are predicted, and the model identifies asymmetries in electric and weak forces, as well as distance- and velocity-dependent interactions. (4) Implications: The framework offers testable predictions for hadron spectroscopy, predicts sterile, exclusive gravitationally interacting bosons as dark-matter candidates, states the equations for the elementary forces, and suggests possible connections between force asymmetries and dark energy.

papers.title: Principle of no paradoxical Universe
papers.abstract: In the standard $Λ\rm CDM$ model, the Universe will keep expanding forever and its lifetime is infinite. Therefore, even the heaviest supermassive black hole will eventually evaporate and the universal occurrence of the black hole information paradox is unavoidable. However, the recent DESI results seem to indicate that dark energy is dynamical and, more importantly, it is possible that the Universe has a finite lifetime and will experience a ``Big Crunch" in some billion years from now. In light of this, the lightest confirmed black hole with mass of order one solar mass may not have a chance to evaporate before the Universe ends. Inspired by these observations, we thus raise an intriguing conjecture: Does the Universe choose a configuration such that the ``in-principle" black hole information paradox can never actually happen in reality? We derive a lower bound on black hole mass as a function of the Universe's lifetime such that the information paradox cannot be realized in nature and some resulting predictions are made. Some profound implications for other related big ideas in physics are briefly discussed.

papers.title: The metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron: parameter-free inflation
papers.abstract: We present a model of slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity, where the connection is independent of the metric. We require that the Einstein-Hilbert term is the only operator that breaks three out of four shift-symmetries of the connection, and impose them on the metric-affine Starobinsky term $αR(Γ)^2$. This replaces it by $α\mathring{R}^2$, the square of the invariant part of the scalar curvature. The theory propagates only the graviton and one healthy scalar, the metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron. Its potential approaches a plateau polynomially, $U\simeq U_0(1-μ^2/χ^2)$, with $μ=\sqrt{6}\,M_P$ fixed by the curvature of the connection. Once $α\simeq2\times10^{8}$ is set by the scalar amplitude, the model has no free parameters. It predicts $n_s\simeq1-3/(2N_*)$ and $r\simeq2\sqrt3\,N_*^{-3/2}$ at leading order in $N_*$, and $n_s=0.968$--$0.974$ and $r=0.011$-$0.008$ with exact slow-roll for $N_*=50$-$60$ $e$-folds. These values agree with current data, and $r$ is within reach of the next generation of $B$-mode measurements.

papers.title: Neutrino Anomalies and Tensions: Experimental Status and Theoretical Interpretations
papers.abstract: Neutrino oscillations successfully describe flavor conversion across a wide range of experiments, yet the origin of several excesses and deficits remains unresolved. This review connects these observations and long-baseline parameter tensions to their proposed physical explanations, clarifying what remains open and how it can be tested. We examine reactor and gallium measurements, accelerator appearance and disappearance searches, and atmospheric constraints, focusing on sterile neutrinos, non-standard interactions, and decoherence in open-system dynamics. For each mechanism, we assess what it modifies, which observations it can address, and which theoretical assumptions and independent constraints limit its viability. Recent results have restricted several interpretations and weakened some earlier tensions; no single extension provides an uncontested account of all observations. We identify the flavor, baseline, energy, and event-topology signatures needed to distinguish competing explanations and assess whether the remaining anomalies require new physics or reflect unresolved flux, interaction, and detector uncertainties.

papers.title: Regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics and non-perturbative renormalization of the shear viscosity of incompressible fluids
papers.abstract: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. By considering an incompressible fluid, we demonstrate explicitly that the regularized theory is UV finite, and therefore admits a continuum limit. Strikingly, the regularized theory of stochastic fluid dynamics is not only amenable to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory, but also to functional methods in the continuum. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.
